papers.title: Sex shapes plasma molecular signatures of dementia risk across APOE ε4 strata
papers.abstract: Sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE {varepsilon}4 groups. The association between APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE {varepsilon}4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers. Most top molecular predictors were subgroup-specific, including C7, CDON and EDIL3 in female carriers and KLK4, MMP12 and TGFBI in male carriers. When UK Biobank models were applied to the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium, 12/17 available top predictors in female carriers and 10/16 in male carriers remained highly ranked. These findings identify distinct molecular signatures of dementia risk across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata, supporting stratified biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Challenges in Quantifying Upper Extremity Dysmetria in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA)
papers.abstract: Background Assessments of upper extremity control in ataxia are susceptible to measurement error and inherent variability. Objectives Quantify trial-to-trial variability in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) nose-to-finger (NTF) and finger chase (FC) tasks, and test agreement between scores derived from live assessment and retrospective video review. Methods 17 patients with cerebellar ataxia were video-recorded performing tasks behind a transparent, calibrated 1-cm grid. NTF tremor amplitude and FC undershoot/overshoot distance derived from live scores were compared with measurements from video review. Results NTF tremor amplitude and FC under/overshoot varied between consecutive trials. Patients received 2.4 {+/-} 0.7 (NTF) and 2.6 {+/-} 0.8 (FC) different SARA scores for limb excursions within one session. Live and video score match was NTF: 64.7% left, 70.6% right; FC: 64.7% left, 41.2% right. Live scoring often overestimated impairment. Conclusions Trial-to-trial variability and live/video discordance limit the precision of SARA upper-limb tasks.

papers.title: Validation of CSF αSyn-SAA in an autopsy cohort with whole-body assessment of Lewy pathology
papers.abstract: Background & Objectives: As recently recommended by neuropathologists, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) alpha-synuclein (-syn) seed amplification assay (SAA) in an autopsy cohort with systemic assessment of Lewy pathology. Methods: CSF was obtained antemortem and stored at -80 . -syn SAA and systemic Lewy pathology assessment were conducted as previously reported. Kinetic parameters, including maximum fluorescence (Fmax) and time to reach 50% of Fmax (T50), were also evaluated. Results: CSF samples were available from 30 patients (8 with symptomatic Lewy body disease [LBD], 2 with multiple system atrophy [MSA], 3 with Alzheimer's disease [AD], and 17 disease controls). Despite different clinical stages, all patients with LBD had diffuse neocortical or limbic-stage pathology at autopsy, with widespread peripheral Lewy bodies, including in the esophagus, heart, and sympathetic ganglia. Lewy pathology was not observed in disease controls. SAA was positive in all 8 with LBD, low positive in one patient with AD, and negative in all others. Fmax was significantly higher in LBD compared with cases without -syn pathology (9091{+/-}2083 vs. 1659{+/-}113 relative fluorescence units). The low-positive case had a lower positivity rate (25% vs. 75-100%), lower Fmax, and longer T50 than LBD cases. Conclusions: In this pilot study, CSF -syn SAA demonstrated high specificity (95%) and high sensitivity (100%) for detecting LBD; however, all LBD cases had widespread pathology, including peripheral involvement. Larger studies are needed to understand the association between CSF -syn SAA and Lewy pathology in the body.

papers.title: MERIT: Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care
papers.abstract: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

papers.title: Assessment of Dissemination in Time in Multiple Sclerosis Using a Single 3D T2-FLAIR magnetic resonance imaging Radiomic Signature
papers.abstract: Background: In multiple sclerosis (MS), dissemination in time (DIT) is an important component of demonstrating disease activity and establishing the chronology of lesion development. DIT is routinely assessed from contrast-enhanced or follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Although proved useful, these methods are not without caveats motivating alternative approaches to study lesion chronology. We investigated whether single T2-FLAIR MRI contains sufficient information to distinguish temporally distinct MS lesion categories using radiomic features. Methods: In a retrospective longitudinal cohort of 273 participants with MS (1,311 MRI acquisitions), persistent brain lesions were temporally stratified using serial T2-FLAIR MRI. Long-standing established (LS-E) lesions were defined as observed for six years at least, and recent incident (R-I), as lesions that appeared over the span of two years in a follow-up MRI and were present until the last scan available. Radiomic features were extracted from lesion-level T2-FLAIR MRI. Feature selection was performed in an independent discovery cohort (Group 1, N=55). Selected features were then used to train a support vector machine classifier in a separate development cohort with repeated group-wise cross-validation (Group 2, N=163). Final performance was assessed in an held-out test cohort (Group 3, N=55). An exploratory analysis was then performed on baseline MRI from 64 subjects with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), acquired after their first clinical demyelinating event. Results: Longitudinal tracking identified 814 classifiable lesions in Group 1, 3203 in Group 2, and 984 in Group 3. In Group 1, 18 radiomic features met predefined selection criteria (FDR-adjusted p smaller than 0.05 and absolute Cohen's d greater than 0.8), spanning intensity, shape, and texture domains. In the independent test cohort, the support vector machine classifier achieved an area under the curve of 0.78, with correct classification rates of 66% for R-I lesions and 73% for LS-E lesions. In the exploratory CIS analysis, predicted lesion temporal composition showed substantial inter-patient heterogeneity, with approximately one in ten participants presenting radiomic features compatible with LS-E lesions at their first clinical event. Conclusions: Single T2-FLAIR MRI contains measurable information related to MS lesion chronology. This proof-of-concept framework supports the feasibility of a line of research based on radiomics temporal lesion characterisation without contrast administration or dense longitudinal follow-up MRI, with potential relevance for studying lesion evolution and supporting DIT assessment.

papers.title: Diagnostic Feature Associations in Atypical Parkinsonian Disorders: A Survey of Movement Disorders Specialists
papers.abstract: Objective: For the atypical parkinsonian disorders (APDs), including dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), multiple system atrophy (MSA), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and corticobasal degeneration (CBD), accurate antemortem diagnosis remains clinically challenging because of overlapping features, phenotypic heterogeneity, and limited definitive biomarkers. Consensus diagnostic criteria are complex and may not reflect how clinicians operationalize diagnostic reasoning in practice. Methods: We surveyed movement disorders specialists regarding diagnostic implications of 32 clinical features, comparing the results with a 2024 consensus algorithmic framework called the "General Neurologist's Practical Diagnostic Algorithm for APDs". We evaluated inter-rater agreement, diagnosis-level framework coverage, feature-level attribution patterns, and exact-set agreement. Results: Respondents demonstrated strong inter-specialist consensus in feature attribution (raw agreement 81.9%; Gwet's AC1 0.67, 95% CI 0.64-0.70). Specialist endorsement increased markedly with framework association strength, from 12.9% to 36.2% to 82.6% for unmapped, modest, and moderate associations respectively. Diagnosis-level coverage was higher for MSA, PSP, and CBD than for DLB. Exact-set agreement was substantially more variable and depended on whether modest associations were incorporated into the framework definition. Despite high self-reported familiarity with and use of published diagnostic criteria, respondents overwhelmingly expressed interest in a unified diagnostic framework for APDs with automated clinical decision support (CDS). Conclusions: Movement disorders specialists showed internally consistent feature-attribution patterns for archetypal features, while differing in the weighting and breadth assigned to weaker or overlapping associations. These findings are evidence for a gap between consensus schemas and specialist diagnostic reasoning and may inform future diagnostic frameworks and CDS approaches for the APDs.

papers.title: Quantitative deep motor phenotyping of 102 people with SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A or SCN8A-related disorders
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Motor dysfunction is a major contributor to disability in pediatric-onset monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet systematic quantifications of motor phenotypes across development using validated clinical scales remain underdeveloped. Existing studies have classified motor phenotypes rather than quantified domain-specific severity, limiting their use as outcome measures in clinical trials. Here, we systematically quantify motor dysfunction using established clinical rating scales to explore their utility as motor endpoints. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, 102 individuals with NDDs (0.5-38 years) secondary to pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in five genes (SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A, SCN8A) and 31 unaffected sibling controls underwent standardized motor assessments using the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale, and the Modified Ashworth Scale. Regional and functional categorization of parameters enabled differentiated interpretation. Gene-specific patterns were evaluated using z-score standardization across the pooled affected cohort, with gene-level averaging and nonparametric bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results: Dysfunction was present in individuals with NDDs across speech (90%), coordination (87%), dystonia (83.3%), gross motor (82.4%) and spasticity (42.2%), with minimal impairment in controls (0-12.9%). We observed substantial heterogeneity across motor domains and subdomains; ataxic dysarthria had the highest score distribution (median 0.83 [IQR, 0.17-1.0]), whereas spasticity showed near-floor scores. Individuals with SCN2A variants demonstrated higher mean z-scores across multiple subdomains than other genes, with more consistent deviations observed in coordination and speech domains (Coordination: mean z = 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.54; Speech: mean z = 0.3, 95% CI 0.03-0.57), whereas domain-specific or less pronounced patterns were observed in other genes. The ataxia and dystonia scales demonstrated low floor and ceiling effects. Discussion: Using three clinical scales across a broad developmental and functional range, our study moves motor phenotyping in monogenic NDDs from categorical description toward quantitative, domain-resolved severity assessment. Exploratory analysis indicates marked heterogeneity in severity profiles across genes, most notably in SCN2A, suggesting potential selective motor vulnerability. These findings provide evidence for the feasibility of motor phenotyping and provide preliminary, cross-sectional benchmark severity distributions. Subsequent longitudinal validation and validation in larger, longitudinal, and variant-stratified cohorts will enable natural history studies and future therapeutic trials alongside seizure outcomes.

papers.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
papers.abstract: Background: Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep -especially deep sleep- could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression. Methods: PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit N=50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham. Discussion: The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS' disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Multi-ancestry rare variant burden analysis of E3 ubiquitin ligase genes in Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome system and have been implicated in early-onset Parkinson's disease (EOPD). We performed a multi-ancestry rare variant burden analysis of seven E3 ubiquitin ligase genes (HERC1, IRF2BPL, KMT2D, RAPSN, RNF168, RNF216, TRIM2) using GP2 Release 11 WGS data from 17,928 PD patients (including 6,659 EOPD) and 8,977 controls across five major ancestry groups (African, Central Asian, East Asian, European, and Middle Eastern). We did not identify any association between gene based rare burden and PD, using the optimised sequence kernel association test (SKAT-O).

papers.title: Head-to-Head Comparison of Flortaucipir and MK6240 tau-PET to Detect Subtle Objective Cognitive Impairment in Clinically Unimpaired Individuals
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Tau-PET is associated with subtle objective cognitive impairment (SOCI) in clinically unimpaired (CU) individuals, but whether the spatial patterns and strengths of these associations differ across tracers remains unclear. We performed a head-to-head comparison of [18F]MK6240 and [18F]flortaucipir to investigate their associations with SOCI in CU individuals. Methods: We cross-sectionally assessed CU participants from the HEAD study who underwent both tau-PET scans. Linear regressions examined associations between domain-specific cognition and tau burden using standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) in regional and voxelwise analyses, alongside regional spatial extent of tauopathy (SEOT) measures. Tau burden was compared across groups representing different levels of SOCI. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education, with additional adjustment for amyloid-beta burden. Centiloid-stratified analyses examined associations across amyloid-beta burden levels. Results: Among 297 participants (mean [SD] age, 67.0 [8.4] years; 179 [60.3%] female), higher [18F]MK6240 SUVR was associated with poorer memory performance. Greater SEOT with either tracer was associated with poorer memory and showed nominal associations with executive dysfunction. Regional association strengths did not differ significantly between tracers, while SEOT yielded comparable or stronger associations than SUVR. Centiloid-stratified analyses revealed tau-cognition associations primarily at intermediate and high amyloid-beta burden. [18F]MK6240 showed more spatially extensive voxelwise associations with memory and across SOCI group comparisons. Regional analyses also yielded more statistically significant differences across SOCI groups with [18F]MK6240 than with flortaucipir. These differences were predominantly driven by participants meeting actuarial mild cognitive impairment criteria, who exhibited greater tau burden than groups with less pronounced psychometric impairment. Across tracers, SEOT yielded more consistently significant differences among SOCI groups than SUVR. Discussion: Both tracers showed associations with SOCI in CU individuals, with broadly comparable regional association strengths despite differences in the spatial extent and statistical significance of their findings. SEOT complemented SUVR by identifying additional significant associations and group differences. These findings suggest that tracer choice and quantification approach may influence the spatial distribution and statistical significance of observed tau-cognition relationships without necessarily altering their overall strength.

papers.title: Tau PET Braak staging across the Alzheimer Disease continuum using Flortaucipir and MK6240
papers.abstract: Tau positron emission tomography (PET) staging is increasingly used to stratify Alzheimers disease (AD), yet cross-tracer interchangeability remains unestablished. In a prospective head-to-head study of 682 individuals across the aging-to-AD continuum, we compared tau PET Braak staging derived from [18F]Flortaucipir and [18F]MK6240. While both tracers showed high internal adherence to hierarchical Braak patterns (89-92%), cross-tracer agreement was limited (43%, weighted {kappa} = 0.54) and fell to 14-23% at early-to-intermediate stages, a key window for therapeutic intervention. Discordance was strongly directional: in over 90% of discordant cases [18F]MK6240 assigned a higher stage, on average approximately one stage above [18F]Flortaucipir. [18F]MK6240 upstaging was associated with greater A{beta} burden, adverse plasma biomarker profiles, and worse cognitive performance. Stage-frequency benchmarking against an external neuropathological cohort (N = 4,422) revealed that PET staging lags neuropathology by ~2 Braak stages for [18F]MK6240 and ~3 for [18F]Flortaucipir in the early phases of disease, with progressive convergence at later stages. Tau PET Braak staging is internally coherent within tracers but not interchangeable across them, with [18F]MK6240 systematically assigning higher stages than [18F]Flortaucipir. This biologically meaningful discordance, most pronounced at early stages, has direct implications for patient selection and staging for clinical trials and practice, necessitating tracer-aware harmonization strategies.

papers.title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
papers.abstract: Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subject's own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.

papers.title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
papers.abstract: Background: Young onset dementia is frequently misdiagnosed, particularly where neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorders (PPD) overlap. Plasma biomarkers measure current pathology, whereas polygenic risk scores (PRS) capture lifelong genetic risk. Whether PRS derived from late-onset and population samples transfer to young-onset presentations, and how they relate to plasma biomarkers, is unknown. Methods: We studied 687 participants of European ancestry from the Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders (MiND) Study, a prospective young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort: 195 healthy controls (HC), 283 PPD, 55 Alzheimers disease (AD) and 154 non-AD neurodegenerative disease (oNDG). PRS for AD, a cross-disorder psychiatric factor (PSY), frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia and Parkinsons disease were computed with PRS CS, excluding the APOE locus. Plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 were available for 332 participants. Models were adjusted for age, sex and APOE e4 dose. Results: Relative to HC, the AD PRS was associated with AD (OR 1.69 per SD, 95% CI 1.17-2.45) but not PPD (0.95, 0.77-1.16). The PSY PRS showed the reciprocal pattern (PPD 1.29, 1.05-1.58; AD 1.00, 0.72-1.40). No PRS was associated with any plasma protein. In distinguishing PPD from oNDG, NfL was the strongest discriminator (OR 2.15, 1.62-2.83). The AD PRS was also associated with oNDG (1.38, 1.11-1.71), without improving discrimination (AUC 0.764 for NfL alone versus 0.773 combined). Conclusion: In young onset presentations, AD and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration. Their combined diagnostic value requires evaluation in larger, longitudinal pre-clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Short intervals of inertial measurement unit data collected during activities of daily living can provide a quantitative method to assess disease severity and functional ability in Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting roughly one million people in the U.S. People with PD (PwPD) exhibit classic motor symptoms that limit performance on functional tasks and reduce quality of life (QOL). Despite functional ability (FA) being a critical indicator of patient well-being, objective and quantitative measurement of FA during activities of daily living (ADLs) is not a part of standard clinical assessments. To address this gap, we conducted a pilot study of PwPD (n = 39) and healthy controls (n = 7) performing ADLs. We attached nine-axis inertial measurement units (IMUs) to toothbrushes and hair combs to collect continuous acceleration and angular velocity data during toothbrushing and hair-combing tasks. After preprocessing, we visualized signals with kernel density estimation and continuous wavelet transforms, revealing characteristic distributional, temporal, and spectral patterns. We then segmented signals into 3-9 second non-overlapping intervals. From each interval, we extracted 30 features (13 acceleration-derived, 17 angular-velocity-derived) and trained eXtreme Gradient Boosted (XGBoost) classifiers to discriminate disease state and severity, symptom presence, and impaired FA. Notably, models trained on hair-combing data discriminated PwPD from controls (balanced accuracy 0.864) and identified patient-reported impairment in FA (0.869). Models trained on toothbrushing data achieved moderate performance on the same tasks (balanced accuracy 0.752 and 0.686, respectively). These preliminary findings suggest that short-segment IMU data from common ADL implements can quantitatively characterize disease severity and task-specific performance in PwPD, supporting their integration into routine clinical care.

papers.title: Increased variability in visual processing in children with autism
papers.abstract: The visual evoked potential (VEP) indexes sensory processing, but the neurophysiological basis of altered VEP amplitudes in autism remains unclear. We examined whether reduced VEP amplitude reflects increased trial-to-trial neural variability and whether this variability relates to electrophysiological markers of cortical excitation/inhibition and developmental functioning. Pattern-reversal VEPs were analyzed in 102 typically developing (TD; 44 female) and 105 autistic (AUT; 15 female) children aged 2-12 years. N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes and inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC) were computed. Resting-state periodic alpha activity and aperiodic exponent were derived using spectral parameterization. Associations among VEP, resting EEG, age, and developmental/behavioral measures were assessed using multiple linear regression. AUT children exhibited reduced N1 amplitude and lower ITPC, with marginally reduced N1-P1 amplitude. Higher ITPC was strongly associated with larger N1 and N1-P1 amplitudes, and group differences in VEP amplitudes were no longer significant after accounting for ITPC. Greater periodic alpha activity was associated with higher ITPC and larger N1-P1 amplitude, while a steeper aperiodic exponent was associated with higher ITPC in the pooled cohort. Within AUT children, higher ITPC was associated with better nonverbal development, verbal cognition, and language scores. Reduced VEP amplitudes in autism may primarily reflect increased trial-to-trial variability rather than systematically weaker stimulus-evoked responses. Associations between ITPC and resting EEG measures suggest that cortical excitation/inhibition may contribute to sensory response reliability. These findings identify neural response consistency as a developmentally relevant feature of visual processing in autism.

papers.title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinson's disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brain's cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a 'vertical' trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel 'lateral trajectory' in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM ('Vertical' target) or its lateral efferent bundle ('Lateral' target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: High-frequency EEG activity moderates the association between amyloid burden and tau in cognitively normal adults
papers.abstract: Background: Resting electroencephalogram (EEG) may capture early excitatory-inhibitory (E-I) imbalance in Alzheimer's disease, but its relationship to beta-amyloid and tau in cognitively normal adults is unclear. Methods: We analyzed resting-state EEG from 24 older adults, 21 cognitively normal (13 beta-amyloid-negative, 8 beta-amyloid-positive) and 3 with MCI/AD (all beta-amyloid-positive), with beta-amyloid positron emission tomography (PET); 20 of the cognitively normal adults also had tau PET. Four parietal measures related to E-I balance and excitability (periodic gamma power, alpha-gamma and theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling [PAC], and the aperiodic exponent) were related to beta-amyloid burden and to early medial temporal lobe (MTL) tau, adjusting for age and sex. Results: In 21 cognitively normal adults, higher beta-amyloid burden was associated with higher parietal periodic gamma power (beta= +0.50, p = 0.025). No E-I measure was associated with MTL tau across all participants. However, in beta-amyloid-positive adults, higher periodic gamma was associated with higher MTL tau, most strongly in the entorhinal cortex (beta = +0.90, p = 0.002), with no association in beta-amyloid-negative adults. Importantly, periodic gamma also moderated the association between beta-amyloid and MTL tau (p = 0.012; consistent across MTL regions after FDR correction). Conclusions: In this pilot study, parietal periodic gamma, an EEG marker of cortical excitability, increased with beta-amyloid burden and was related to MTL tau only in the presence of beta-amyloid. Periodic gamma is a candidate marker of beta-amyloid-related E-I imbalance that warrants confirmation in larger samples.

papers.title: Benefit Expectations and Neuroprotective Prescribing for Acute Ischemic Stroke in China
papers.abstract: BackgroundNeuroprotective therapies are frequently used for acute ischemic stroke in China. We examined associations of neurologists self-rated familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations with reported prescribing frequency. MethodsA hospital-based quota survey recruited attending-level or senior neurologists involved in acute ischemic stroke care across mainland China from May 27 to July 16, 2025. High-frequency use was defined as prescribing neuroprotective therapy to at least 60% of patients. High familiarity and importance were ratings of 4 or 5 on 5-level scales; consistently high benefit expectations required ratings of 4 or 5 in all 4 scenarios. Modified Poisson generalized estimating equations estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with hospital-clustered robust standard errors. ResultsAmong 1982 neurologists from 251 hospitals, 1007 (50.8%) were men and 1745 (88.0%) practiced in tertiary hospitals. High-frequency use was reported by 1596 respondents (80.5%), high familiarity by 1006 (50.8%), and consistently high benefit expectations by 1290 (65.1%). Lower familiarity with high-frequency use was reported by 743 respondents (37.5%). High familiarity (adjusted PR, 1.053; 95% CI, 1.007-1.102), high perceived importance (adjusted PR, 1.294; 95% CI, 1.148-1.458), and consistently high benefit expectations (adjusted PR, 1.198; 95% CI, 1.131-1.269) were associated with high-frequency use after adjustment for demographic and professional characteristics. ConclusionsFrequent self-reported neuroprotective prescribing coexisted with lower self-rated familiarity in a substantial subgroup. Familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations were associated with prescribing frequency. These cross-sectional, class-level measures cannot establish prescribing appropriateness or causality. Studies linking drug-specific observed prescribing to indications and patient outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with amyloid accumulation over 3 years in cognitively healthy adults
papers.abstract: ImportanceIdentifying potentially modifiable risk factors for Alzheimers disease (AD) is a priority. Repetitive negative thinking (RNT) is a modifiable cognitive-emotional process common to many psychological risk factors for AD, including anxiety and depression. The psychological debt hypothesis proposes that RNT may itself increase risk for AD. ObjectiveTo determine whether RNT symptoms are associated with change in established neurobiological markers of AD risk over time. DesignLongitudinal neuroimaging study with the IMAP/IMAP+ cohort. SettingMonocentric with community-dwelling participants. Participants94 cognitively healthy adults aged 21-89 years (average 57.41 SD 18.31, 55% female) with up to 3 neuroimaging scans over a 3-year period. ExposureAll participants completed validated measures of RNT, anxiety and depression symptoms. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s)Change over time in global cortical amyloid (Florbetapir-PET), glucose metabolism (FDG-PET), and structural grey matter volume (MRI) adjusted for potential confounders. PET images were corrected for partial volume effects, and AD-relevant masks were used for all neuroimaging outcomes. Post-hoc analyses divided the predictor variable into tertiles to aid visualisation, and FDR-corrected voxel-wise analyses were performed to identify region-specific changes. ResultsRNT was associated with increasing global amyloid accumulation even after controlling for psychological symptoms (B = 0.0120, 95% Confidence Interval 0.003 to 0.021, P = 0.012), and in sensitivity analyses limited to participants aged [≥]50 or [≥]60. Post-hoc tests showed a significant difference in rate of amyloid accumulation between the lowest and highest RNT tertiles (P=0.008). Voxelwise analyses revealed that RNT predicted significantly faster increases in regions vulnerable to early amyloid accumulation in AD (e.g. precuneus, posterior cingulate cortex, and medial frontal cortex). RNT was not associated with change in glucose metabolism or brain atrophy (Ps>0.05). Neither anxiety nor depressive symptoms were associated with change in any neuroimaging outcome (Ps>0.05). Conclusions and RelevanceHigher RNT was associated with more rapid accumulation of cortical amyloid in regions affected early in AD. These findings indicate that this transdiagnostic cognitive-emotional process may be an early marker and/or driver of AD pathology. Given that RNT is responsive to treatment, future research is needed to investigate whether modifying RNT reduces AD risk.

papers.title: Relative Importance of Positive and Potentially Traumatic Childhood Experiences in Explaining Multiple Sclerosis Symptoms
papers.abstract: The original adverse childhood experiences study linked childhood experiences to health in adulthood. Since then, other traumatic and adverse childhood experiences (TRACEs) and positive childhood experiences (PCEs) have also been linked to physical and mental health. However, little research has examined these experiences among people with Multiple Sclerosis (MS). This study examined whether cumulative and individual childhood experiences explained variability in symptom burden in adults with MS. Participants were 467 adults with MS (Mage = 41.5, 45% female) who completed measures of pain, subjective cognitive impairment, cognitive fatigue, depression, TRACEs, and PCEs. The elastic net algorithm examined cumulative TRACEs, PCEs, their interaction, and individual childhood experiences. R-squared was used to assess the proportion of variance in each outcome accounted for by childhood experiences, and variable importance identified experiences that most improved the models explanatory power for each outcome. Individual childhood experiences accounted for 26.0%, 17.1%, 13.9%, and 22.4% of variance in pain, subjective cognitive impairment, cognitive fatigue, and depression, respectively, and overall had stronger performance relative to the cumulative main effects TRACEs and PCEs model, and their interaction. Having at least one safe caregiver was consistently important across MS symptoms, and sudden loss of a loved one had the strongest explanatory association with subjective cognitive impairment and cognitive fatigue specifically. Specific childhood experiences accounted for meaningful variance in the MS symptom burden. Individual childhood experiences provided more explanatory information than cumulative scores. Findings support examining specific TRACEs and PCEs when investigating symptom burden in MS.

papers.title: Quantitative CTA-Based Carotid Plaque Composition Across Stroke Etiologies and Residual Vascular Risk
papers.abstract: BackgroundCarotid plaque vulnerability features may provide prognostic information beyond luminal stenosis, but the value of quantitative plaque composition on CTA remains unclear. ObjectivesWe investigated whether plaque composition analysis in routine CTA in patients with ischemic stroke or TIA can identify high-risk plaques across etiologies, particularly among strokes of undetermined etiology and predict residual vascular risk. MethodsWe analyzed carotid CTAs from 314 patients with acute ischemic stroke or TIA. CTA-derived plaque composition was quantified using commercially available software and compared between ipsilateral and contralateral plaques across etiology groups. Associations of plaque characteristics with subsequent vascular events were assessed using Cox regression models. ResultsAmong patients with ischemic events of undetermined etiology, ipsilateral plaques showed significant enrichment for greater LRNC volume (ratio, 1.97; 95% CI, 1.22-3.18), an association that persisted after adjustment for wall volume (ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-1.99). During a median 3-year follow-up, larger LRNC volume was associated with subsequent vascular events in patients with ischemic stroke of undetermined etiology (HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.12-3.43), as were calcification, noncalcified matrix, and total wall volumes. Associations for individual plaque components attenuated after adjustment for wall volume. ConclusionsCTA-derived LRNC is enriched in carotid plaques ipsilateral to ischemic events of undetermined etiology and is associated with future vascular risk. Quantitative CTA-based plaque assessment may provide complementary information for etiologic evaluation and vascular risk stratification.

papers.title: Blood-based biomarkers across the Alzheimer's disease continuum in older Korean population
papers.abstract: BackgroundPlasma phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) is a robust biomarker of Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology. However, whether a single biomarker can adequately capture both clinical diagnosis and disease progression remains unclear. We investigated the complementary roles of plasma AD biomarkers and routinely measured metabolic markers across different stages of AD. MethodsUsing the Gwangju Alzheimers & Related Dementia (GARD) cohort, we analyzed cross-sectional and longitudinal data, including amyloid-PET, MRI, neuropsychological examinations, and APOE genotypes. Plasma pTau217, GFAP, and NfL levels were measured alongside routine biochemical markers to evaluate their associations with pathology and neurodegeneration. ResultsPlasma pTau217 best identified amyloid-PET positivity (AUC > 0.91). For AD diagnosis, adding cholesterol and glucose to pTau217 improved the AUC from 0.781 to 0.873. To predict progression in amyloid-positive individuals, glucose alone outperformed pTau217 (AUC 0.840 vs. 0.747), whereas adding GFAP yielded the strongest prognostic performance (AUC 0.867). DiscussionPlasma pTau217 primarily reflects amyloid pathology, whereas metabolic markers provide complementary information related to the clinical expression and progression of the disease. Integrating biomarkers across distinct biological domains may improve risk stratification and prognostic assessment in AD.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography
papers.abstract: Background and PurposeSpreading depolarizations (SDs) are waves of near-complete breakdown of the transmembrane ion gradients that underlie migraine aura and occur in patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic, ischemic or hemorrhagic brain injury. SDs are involved in primary and secondary brain injury. They are associated with poor neurological outcome and represent a modifiable therapeutic target. However, despite decades of investigation, SD detection still requires invasive subdural electrocorticography (ECoG) using an implanted subdural electrode strip, restricting monitoring to a small subset of neurosurgical patients. MethodsWe developed WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp electroencephalography (EEG) biomarker of SD based on spatiotemporal propagation characteristics of delta-band EEG activity. The biomarker was trained and validated using concurrent, multi-day scalp EEG and invasive subdural electrocorticography recordings from patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or malignant hemispheric stroke (MHS) across three institutions. We assessed out-of-sample performance across institutions, diagnosis, and surgical approaches, as well as calibration, temporal synchrony, and spatial specificity relative to gold-standard SDs annotated on ECoG. Clinical utility was further evaluated in 607 patients comatose after cardiac arrest from the multicenter International Cardiac Arrest REsearch (I-CARE) consortium, a population in whom invasive monitoring is not performed. Outcome analyses excluded patients who died (Cerebral Performance Category [CPC] 5) because death may reflect decisions to withdraw life-sustaining treatment in addition to neurological injury. ResultsA total of 1,119 gold-standard SDs were annotated in 32 patients (TBI, n=17; SAH, n=12; MHS, n=3; range 0-187 SDs per patient). Across exhaustive cross-validation and institution-, diagnosis-, and surgical approach-based hold-out analyses, WAVEFRONT models trained on one set of patients consistently maintained high performance when evaluated in previously unseen out-of-group cohorts. At the optimal operating point, WAVEFRONT achieved a mean cross-validated true positive rate of 97.3{+/-}1% with a false positive rate of 6.0{+/-}0.5%, calculated over 2-min sliding windows with 30-s overlaps. The cumulative duration of WAVEFRONT detections within 30-hour windows strongly correlated with the number of SDs measured by invasive ECoG (R2=0.7411). Scalp-detected depressions were spatially consistent with the location of the invasive recording strip, and visual inspection demonstrated close temporal correspondence with invasive detections, including during SD clusters. External validation in the independent I-CARE cohort using WAVEFRONT trained on the invasive-monitoring cohort demonstrated significantly greater SD burden on day 3 of post-arrest EEG monitoring among patients with poor neurological outcome (CPC 3-4, n=29) than those with good outcome (CPC 1-2, n=225; p=0.007). ConclusionsEight decades after Leaos description of SD in 1944, we propose and validate a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of SD. Consistent performance across institution-, diagnosis-, and surgical approach-based hold-out analyses, together with burden calibration, spatial specificity, and temporal synchrony with ECoG detections, supports the validity of the WAVEFRONT framework. The association of biomarker burden with neurologic outcome after cardiac arrest suggests that noninvasive monitoring may enable investigation of spreading depolarizations in populations where invasive monitoring is not feasible. Future studies should evaluate prospective performance, treatment responsiveness, and disease-specific associations of the SD biomarker with clinical outcome.

papers.title: Same pipelines, different answers: how evaluation design shapes EEG seizure prediction
papers.abstract: Seizure-prediction studies on scalp electroencephalography (EEG) often report accuracies that would be clinically useful, yet the score a model receives also depends on how its test data were separated from its training data. We kept five published pipelines fixed, from a spectral baseline (power spectral density with linear discriminant analysis, PSD+LDA) to a transformer, and changed only how they were evaluated on the CHB-MIT database. When whole subjects were held out in 20 repeated partitions, every pipeline scored close to the 0.5 reference (mean area under the ROC curve, AUC, 0.527-0.553), and the five pipelines differed less from one another than each varied between partitions. Within patients, PSD+LDA reached an AUC of 0.815 when windows were allocated at random but 0.572 when each preictal block was kept intact and later seizures were held out for testing. Tracing every window back to its recording showed that an index-based within-patient split had let raw EEG samples cross the train-test boundary in all ten eligible cases. Thresholds tuned to allow 1.67% false positives on validation data did not hold that rate on new subjects, and at those thresholds only 2-6% of preictal windows were detected. A zero-shot test of the baseline on the Siena database gave an AUC of 0.480. In this benchmark, the choice of evaluation changed the answer far more than the choice of architecture. We release the window manifests, partitions and predictions so that new models can be tested on the same terms. All results concern retrospective window classification, not continuous alarms.

papers.title: Brain Dynamics of Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness at Rest Reveal Alterations in Multisensory and Motor Areas
papers.abstract: BackgroundPersistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is a chronic functional disorder with unsteadiness and postural instability, attributed to altered multisensory integration and visual dependence. fMRI studies report altered connectivity in several regions, however, dynamic connectivity remains unexplored. ObjectivesWe characterized resting-state brain dynamics in 17 patients with PPPD and 20 matched healthy controls (HC), and their relationship to clinical and postural measures. MethodsCo-Activation Patterns (CAPs) were derived from resting-state fMRI scans for four seeds relevant to multisensory integration, motor output and vestibular processing - right temporo-parietal junction (rTPJ), caudate nucleus, hippocampus and operculo-parietal area 2 (OP2) - and their temporal metrics compared between groups. Partial Least Squares Correlation (PLSC) related CAPs to mood, vertigo, stress, and visual dependence for gait and postural control. ResultsPatients with PPPD showed altered dynamics seeded from rTPJ (decrease of a salience-coupled CAP, increased entries into a visual/dorsal-attention-coupled CAP), caudate nucleus (increased time in a default mode-coupled CAP, decrease of a salience/visual-coupled CAP) and hippocampus (increase of a default-mode-coupled CAP), but not OP2. PLSC yielded two significant latent components: the first linked rTPJ, OP2 and hippocampal CAPs sharing visual network co-deactivation to stress, mood, vertigo and visual dependence for gait; the second linked all caudate and two rTPJ CAPs to postural sway with eyes closed (visual dependence). Individual brain-behavior scores correlated in both groups. ConclusionResting-state dynamics are altered in multisensory and motor regions in PPPD, but preserved in OP2, the core vestibular cortex. Brain-behavior organization appears shared across groups, with shifted dynamics in patients. Graphical abstractCurved arrows indicate dynamic functional connectivity patterns (Co-Activation Patterns) differing between patients with PPPD and HC (the direction is indicated by the small straight arrows). Dashed arrows indicate latent components of brain-behavior coupling identified through PLSC analysis. (rTPJ: right temporo-parietal junction; OP2: parietal operculum area 2; AP: antero-posterior). papers.title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms
papers.abstract: Identifying individuals at risk for neurodegeneration is a priority for clinical trials. Parkinsons Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) deploys strategies to enroll individuals before typical clinical Parkinsons disease symptoms: recruiting polysomnogram-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and central identification of hyposmia via smell testing. Groups were divided into RBD with and without hyposmia (RBD+Hyposmia, RBD-Hyposmia) and hyposmia with and without self-reported dream enactment behavior (Hyposmia+DEB, Hyposmia-DEB). Participants underwent clinical and biomarker testing including CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay (CSFaSynSAA) and dopamine transporter imaging. While all enrollment strategies showed robust enrichment for CSFaSynSAA positivity, RBD+Hyposmia and Hyposmia+DEB were more likely CSFaSynSAA+ (94% and 85%) vs RBD-Hyposmia (40%) and Hyposmia-DEB (55%). Among CSFaSynSAA+, RBD+Hyposmia and Hyposmia+DEB had more mood, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms than Hyposmia-DEB. PPMI identified a large biologically-defined early neuronal synucleinopathy cohort and demonstrated biomarker and multi-domain clinical heterogeneity within CSFaSynSAA+ individuals prior to symptom onset.

papers.title: CSF Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers in Relation to Functional Status and Tofersen Treatment Response in ALS
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease primarily affecting motor neurons but also frequently involving cognitive impairment. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) measurements of {beta}-amyloid peptides (A{beta}40, A{beta}42), tau proteins, and neurofilaments are clinically established biomarkers in neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimers disease (AD). Emerging evidence suggests that AD-related pathological changes and AD-related biomarkers may appear in ALS, yet their diagnostic and prognostic significance remains unclear. In this retrospective study, we analyzed clinical and CSF biomarker data from patients with ALS, AD, Huntingtons disease (HD), and other disease controls recruited in real-world clinical settings. The dataset comprised A{beta}40, A{beta}42, total tau (t-Tau), phosphorylated tau181 (pTau181), phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), and relevant serum markers. Additionally, longitudinal CSF sampling over one year was evaluated in three ALS patients receiving tofersen treatment. In this real-world cohort, AD-related CSF biomarkers demonstrated no diagnostic value for distinguishing ALS from other neurodegenerative conditions. However, A{beta}40, A{beta}42, and pTau181 levels correlated positively with ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) global score and serum Creatine Kinase MB (CK-MB) concentrations. At the same time, a higher A{beta}42/A{beta}40 ratio was associated with better memory performance on the Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen (ECAS). In tofersen-treated cases, AD-related biomarkers gradually declined during follow-up. These findings suggest that elevated CSF AD-associated biomarkers in ALS may reflect preserved functional and cognitive status and exhibited parallel declines during follow-up in three tofersen-treated patients, supporting their further prospective evaluation as exploratory markers of therapeutic responsiveness. papers.title: Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living Deep Phenotyping and Longitudinal
papers.abstract: ObjectiveMyasthenia gravis clinical trials increasingly rely on the MG Activities of Daily Living total score to assess disease severity and treatment response. However, aggregate scores may obscure clinically meaningful changes in individual symptom domains. To determine whether item-level MG-Activities of Daily Living profiles identify distinct clinical phenotypes and whether longitudinal phenotype transitions reveal disease changes inadequately captured by aggregate scores. MethodsMG-Activities of Daily Living evaluations from seven clinical trials and observational studies (5,259 observations were analyzed using principal component analysis and K-medoids clustering with Cityblock distance. Longitudinal phenotype transitions were evaluated in the three longitudinal cohorts and compared with changes in total scores. ResultsDespite low median MG-ADL scores (2.0-3.0), substantial intercohort symptom heterogeneity was observed. Clustering identified five phenotypes: mild ocular (23.7%), severe ocular-dominant (23.5%), bulbar-respiratory dominant (22.6%), severe generalized (16.0%), and proximal limb-axial weakness (14.3%). Longitudinal phenotype instability occurred in 38-49% of Explore participants, 47-49% of Promise participants, and 20-25% of MGTX participants. Importantly, clinically meaningful phenotype transitions, including shifts from ocular to bulbar predominance, frequently occurred with changes of only one point in total MG-ADL scores. Conversely, substantial total score fluctuations could occur without a change in phenotype. InterpretationMG-ADL total scores incompletely characterize disease heterogeneity and longitudinal symptom evolution. Incorporating item-level phenotyping into clinical trials and routine care may improve interpretation of treatment response, identify clinically important deterioration overlooked by aggregate scores, and facilitate more precise assessment of disease trajectories.

papers.title: The Portland SEEQ: A Harmonizable Questionnaire for Environmental Exposome Profiling in Prodromal Synucleinopathy
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe development of the Portland Suspected Environmental Exposures Questionnaire (SEEQ) and its initial application for environmental exposome profiling in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). BackgroundEnvironmental exposures may contribute to Parkinson disease and related synucleinopathies, yet existing instruments variably capture specific agents, co-exposures, exposure uncertainty, timing, and mitigating factors. MethodsSEEQ was iteratively developed to assess pesticides, solvents/industrial chemicals, welding fumes, heavy metals, residential and occupational exposures, and relevant lifestyle factors. Direct exposures were classified as definite, probable, possible, or uncertain/unlikely, with additional assessment of frequency/duration, life stage, and protective-equipment use. SEEQ was administered to participants with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD. Exposure prevalence, co-exposure patterns, and exploratory associations with clinical phenotypes and longitudinal progression were examined. ResultsEighty-three participants completed SEEQ; 81 (97.6%) completed all four direct exposure domains. Definite/probable exposure was reported for pesticides in 38.6%, solvents/industrial chemicals in 43.4%, welding fumes in 21.0%, and heavy metals in 34.1%. Among complete responders, 60.5% reported [≥]1 and 42.0% [≥]2 direct exposure domains. Forty-five participants identified [≥]1 named agent or mixture. Greater exposure burden was cross-sectionally associated most consistently with greater autonomic symptom burden, but was not associated with longitudinal clinical worsening. ConclusionSEEQ provides a practical, multidomain framework for structured environmental exposome profiling in prodromal synucleinopathy. Larger studies with external exposure validation and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Brain-Derived pTau217 and Plasma Proteomic Profiles Across Cognitive and Dementia Groups in Congolese Older Adults
papers.abstract: Blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer disease and related dementias have been validated largely in populations of European ancestry. We characterized plasma proteins in 786 adults aged 65 years or older in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, classified as cognitively unimpaired, mild cognitive impairment, suspected Alzheimer disease, mixed dementia, or vascular dementia. Proteins were quantified with the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120. Sex showed the strongest associations with protein expression, followed by age, whereas APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status was associated with four measures. MME was downregulated across all dementia groups and showed the largest effect in each dementia-versus-CU comparison. A random forest model combining 10 biomarkers with age, sex, and APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status achieved a mean cross-validated area under the curve of 0.768, compared with 0.612 for brain-derived pTau217 alone. Because biomarker selection and ranking were performed using the full dataset before cross-validation, model performance may be optimistic. These findings support demographic adjustment and population-specific validation of plasma biomarkers and identify MME as a hypothesis-generating signal for further study.
